acceptance_criteria: New module `stl` in `swx-io` with `pub fn write_stl_binary(positions: &[[f32; 3]], indices: &[u32], out: &mut impl std::io::Write) -> Result<(), StlError>` and `pub fn write_stl_ascii(name: &str, positions: &[[f32; 3]], indices: &[u32], out: &mut impl std::io::Write) -> Result<(), StlError>`, both documented with the format description they follow.
Each facet normal is the unit normal `normalize((b - a) × (c - a))` of its three vertices in index order. A degenerate (zero-area) triangle gets the normal `[0, 0, 0]` and is still written.
Binary output: the 80-byte header is fixed text (not a timestamp), so writing the same input twice gives byte-identical output; its length is exactly `84 + 50 × triangles`.

`StlError` is a documented enum with variants for an index count that is not a multiple of 3, an index out of range (naming the index and the vertex count), a non-finite coordinate, and an I/O error. Nothing panics on bad input.

Tests (no files needed, write to a `Vec<u8>`): a unit cube of 12 triangles gives 684 binary bytes with all 12 normals axis-aligned and pointing out of the cube; the ASCII output of one triangle equals an exact expected string; both formats agree on the vertices; each `StlError` case; a degenerate triangle; byte-identical double write.
No `unsafe`, and `swx-io` still has no workspace dependencies. `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` is not edited.
`cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test --workspace` pass.
QA report (FACTORY §6b) posted on the PR.
objective.description: M4-02a: swx-io: binary and ASCII STL writers for an indexed triangle mesh
